biftu-quarry-mizan-dima-road.whole: At the credit's closing the Bank's completion report counts 305 km of the 434.5 km of road targeted as improved, rising to 320 km once the Mizan-Dima road was finished in April 2019. Kombolcha-Burka-Mille was complete at 133 km, Mizan-Dima had reached 77 km of 92 and Konso-Yabello 95 km of 105, and the Ambo-Wolliso and Debre Birhan-Ankober contracts were terminated. The share of rural land within 2 km of an all-season road rose from 17.8 to 36.9 per cent against a target of 40 per cent. Direct beneficiaries were counted at 1,983,354 against a target of 2,325,900 and a baseline already at 1,943,400, which the report calls marginally achieved at 10 per cent of the intended increase. Average travel speed on the finished sections reached 70 km/h against a target of 80; travel and turnaround time for heavy goods vehicles on the Addis-Mille-Djibouti route stayed at six days, which the report attributes to deterioration on the rest of the route, mostly inside Djibouti. The report's after-the-fact calculation puts the Mizan-Dima road's economic rate of return at 32.4 per cent against 15.1 per cent estimated at appraisal. It says that figure is built from road agency costs and road users' vehicle operating and travel time costs over 20 years, so it counts no payment to anyone moved or compensated. All of these are the Bank's own figures. Its Independent Evaluation Group, the Bank's internal evaluators, reviewed them in January 2020 and gave the same ratings as the report: Moderately Unsatisfactory for the outcome, Unsatisfactory for Bank performance and Modest for the quality of monitoring. No independent check was found.

No non-Bank account of what the roads delivered was found.

caldwell-bridge-liberia-compensation.whole: The Bank's completion report counts 24 km of Monrovia city streets and 148.5 km of rural road on the Cotton Tree-Buchanan and Pleebo-Barclayville corridors rehabilitated, and a new road intersection at the Vai Town Bridge. Maintenance was done on 45.5 km of previously repaired rural road against a revised target of 131.6 km and an original target of 641 km, the shortfall following the cancellation of two misprocured lots. A new fuel unloading facility at the Port of Monrovia was built but was not in service when the project closed. Average travel time between Cotton Tree and Buchanan fell from 163 minutes to 55, and between Pleebo and Barclayville from 160 to 45. The share of Monrovia streets rated good or fair went from 5 to 35 per cent, and 94 per cent of the rural population was recorded as living within reach of an all-season road against a revised target of 90 per cent; the same review cites a separate Bank spatial analysis putting Liberia's rural accessibility index at 48 per cent, up from 40. The report puts the number of people who benefited at 1,194,729 against a revised target of 744,980, counted by drawing a 10 km band around the roads and assuming the whole population of Monrovia gained from the urban works. It gives an economic rate of return of 18 per cent, covering 86 per cent of project cost, with none calculated at appraisal. All the figures are the Bank's own. Its Independent Evaluation Group, the Bank's internal evaluators, kept the report's Satisfactory outcome rating but lowered its rating of the Bank's own performance from Highly Satisfactory to Satisfactory, citing shortcomings in monitoring. No independent check was found.

chebei-village-guangzhou-resettlement.whole: The project built or expanded three domestic wastewater treatment plants in Guangzhou with a combined capacity of 475,000 cubic metres a day. The Bank's completion report says this took the share of the city's wastewater that is treated from 50 to 97 per cent against a target of 90 per cent; the Independent Evaluation Group, the Bank's internal evaluators, puts the project's plants at about a fifth of Guangzhou's treatment capacity. A hazardous waste treatment facility was enlarged during construction from a planned 150,000 to 290,000 cubic metres. It was not running when the completion report was written, began operating in August 2013 under a three-year private contract, and had treated about 9,000 tonnes by the time the review was posted, against the report's target of 45,000 tonnes a year. Average sewerage tariffs went from Rmb 0.70 to Rmb 1.07 per cubic metre, against a project target of Rmb 1.50 and an estimated Rmb 2.94 needed to cover operating costs and depreciation. Spending reached US$520.8 million against US$431.9 million estimated at appraisal, an increase the review says the government met entirely, and no economic rate of return was calculated at appraisal or at completion. Both documents are the Bank's. The review's lower outcome rating, and its cut of Bank performance from the report's Moderately Satisfactory to Moderately Unsatisfactory, rest on three grounds: the project's investments came to about 6 per cent of the US$8.5 billion the government was spending at the same time on the Pearl River clean-up; two of three planned inter-municipal pilots were completed and the regional master plan was not implemented; and the improvement in river water samples, about 70 per cent meeting Class III against a 58 per cent baseline and an 80 per cent target, cannot be attributed to the project. No independent check was found.

cuijiaying-han-river-resettlement.whole: The complex carries six turbines with 90 MW of installed capacity. The Bank's completion report says it generated 431 GWh in 2010, with about 446 GWh expected in a normal year, and equates that to about 322,800 tonnes of carbon dioxide avoided. The dam adds roughly 40 million tonnes of live storage for Xiangfan municipality and for 118,000 hectares of irrigated land in the Tangdong farmland region. Thirty-three kilometres of waterway upstream of the complex were improved so that vessels of up to 1,000 tonnes and tows of two to four barges can use them, and lock availability reached 95 per cent against a target of 85. The project team told the Independent Evaluation Group, the Bank's internal evaluators, that inland waterway traffic in the Xiangfan area was 5.61 million tonnes in 2010 against 3.66 million tonnes in the 2003 base year. Spending came to US$254.2 million against US$211.1 million estimated at appraisal. The report's economic rate of return was 21.3 per cent at completion against 22.2 per cent estimated at appraisal, covering 99 per cent of project cost; the cost per kilowatt of capacity installed was US$2,132 against a target of US$2,150. Every figure here is the Bank's or its borrower's. No independent check was found.

guiguang-railway-land-acquisition.whole: The line was built: 847 km of double-track electrified passenger railway from Guiyang to Guangzhou, with 342 bridges and viaducts and 233 tunnels, and 21 stations against a target of 30. The Bank's completion report says average travel time between the two ends fell from 1,500 minutes to 251, an 83 per cent cut that beat the original target of 330 minutes, and that express passenger trains went from three pairs a day to 25 against targets of 15 and later 20. It was decided not to run freight on the line, so the added capacity is for passengers only. A survey of 467 passengers on 12 trains at closing found 61 per cent travelling as tourists and 36 per cent on business, over 40 per cent with monthly incomes of 4,000 yuan or less, and 36 per cent saying they would not have made the trip without the line. The Bank's US$299.5 million loan sat inside a project costed at US$12.53 billion at appraisal and US$13.05 billion at closing. That is about US$14 million per kilometre, which the report, citing a Bank study of Chinese railway construction costs, calls among the lowest in the world. The report's economic rate of return was 18 per cent at completion against 16 per cent at appraisal, covering 74 per cent of project cost and built from travel time and distance savings, freed capacity on existing lines, and fewer road accidents and emissions. All the figures are the Bank's own. The Independent Evaluation Group, the Bank's internal evaluators, also raised the risk to the outcome from the report's Negligible to Modest, over the financial viability of the newly created line company. No independent check was found.

Both print the same output and traffic figures. The outcome ratings are already on the card, so only the risk rating is given here. No non-Bank account of what the line delivered was found.

guiyang-youxiao-road-resettlement.whole: The project built 7.04 km of urban road designed for 60 km/h, 11 stretches of rural road, 15 rural bus terminals and a freight depot. The Bank's completion report says Youxiao Road cut travel between the Longdongbao area and downtown Guiyang, which mountains had separated from the core urban area, and the project team told the Independent Evaluation Group, the Bank's internal evaluators, that the saving was 21 minutes. In the rural area 67 more administrative villages were linked by all-weather roads, the new bus terminals serve 118 administrative villages, and a survey covering a quarter of the project's rural roads found average travel time on them down from 39.8 to 25.8 minutes. The report also credits the road with drawing Rmb 528 million of investment into Bixiang Town after it opened in 2013, a 192 per cent rise on 2009, and a 129.2 per cent rise in that township's revenue; it also records that most of the bus terminals and freight depots are not well operated and maintained. Spending reached US$360.7 million against US$314.4 million estimated before appraisal, and the report's economic rate of return was 16 per cent at completion against 16.9 per cent at appraisal, covering over 99 per cent of project cost. Every figure here is the Bank's own. The Independent Evaluation Group rated the quality of the completion report itself Unsatisfactory. No independent check was found.
guiyang-youxiao-road-resettlement.searched: World Bank completion report ICR2512 for P093963 and the Independent Evaluation Group's ICR Review, posted 28 October 2014, both read from the PDFs. The 16.9 and 16 per cent returns are appraisal and completion estimates of the same quantity. himachal-pradesh-state-roads-debris.whole: Alongside the upgraded roads, the Bank's completion report counts periodic maintenance awarded on 1,831 km against a target of about 2,000 km, 25 accident blackspots treated against a target of 20, and a road accident database running in every district of the state by July 2015. It says average speeds on the upgraded roads rose from 29 to 40 km/h, an increase of 38 per cent against a 25 per cent target, that the share of the state's core network in poor condition fell from 40 per cent to 10.4 per cent, and that deaths in traffic accidents per 1,000 vehicles fell from 0.28 in 2014 to 0.21 in 2017. No outcome indicator for transport costs was set when the project was appraised, so a proxy was used at closing: average vehicle operating cost of 9.78 rupees per kilometre against a pre-project 14.39, a 32 per cent reduction. The state did not create the road fund the project had planned, and the share of permanent gang labour in maintenance spending fell only from 75 to 62 per cent against a 50 per cent target. All these figures are the Bank's. The report's economic rate of return was 26 per cent at completion, covering 88 per cent of project cost, against 27 per cent at appraisal covering 78 per cent. The Independent Evaluation Group, the Bank's internal evaluators, agreed with the Moderately Satisfactory outcome rating and with the Moderately Satisfactory rating of Bank performance, but rated the project's efficiency Modest in spite of that return because of the cost and time overruns, and cut the rating of the project's monitoring from Substantial to Modest. No independent check was found.

huai-river-flood-drainage-resettlement.whole: The Bank's completion report counts 444.62 km of dikes strengthened against a target of 417.45 km, 1,023.51 km of river dredged against 980.54 km, 252 irrigation and drainage pumping stations against 182, 487 sluice gates and culverts against 427, 250 bridges against 197, 140.88 km of drainage ditches dug or rehabilitated, and 36 farmer-run drainage and irrigation associations set up. It reports 9,682.4 square kilometres of rural and urban land protected from flooding against a target of 9,576.2, and 7.43 million people protected against a target of 6.64 million. Agricultural income per head rose by RMB 260 a year against a target of RMB 233; commerce across the four provinces grew by RMB 263.33 million against a target of RMB 118.41 million; and flood-related losses of crops and property fell by RMB 797.99 million against a target of RMB 699.45 million. The Bank's US$200 million loan sat inside a project costed at US$597.41 million at appraisal and US$613.77 million at completion, and the report's economic rate of return was 25 per cent at completion against 20 per cent at appraisal, covering 61 per cent of project cost. All the figures are the Bank's own. The Independent Evaluation Group, the Bank's internal evaluators, gave the same outcome, Bank performance and borrower performance ratings as the report, and prints the risk to the outcome as Modest where the report used the word Moderate. It recorded that the report's further claim that losses fell because flood control let people diversify into aquaculture was not documented. No independent check was found.

jituhun-railway-resettlement.whole: The line was built: 360 km of double-track electrified passenger railway from Jilin to Hunchun designed for 250 km/h, with 90.96 km of track on 115 bridges and viaducts and 155.7 km inside 85 tunnels, and a 3.3 km four-track bridge over a highway and the Songhua River. Eight stations were built; two of them, DashitouNan and Weihuling, had not been opened when the project closed. Trains run at a maximum of 200 km/h to save energy. The Bank's completion report says transit time between Tumen and Jilin fell from 460 minutes to 113, that train pairs a day on the corridor rose to 26 against a target of 13, and that the line carried 8.2 million passengers past a fixed measuring point against a target of 8 million. It also records that traffic density in 2016 was about 24 per cent below the appraisal estimate, and a survey of 500 passengers found 17 per cent who would not have travelled without the line and 83 per cent who would have used another mode. The Bank lent US$200 million, of which US$198.7 million was drawn, inside a project estimated at US$6.30 billion at appraisal and costing US$5.27 billion, 86 per cent of that estimate, after design changes to the track and the dropping of the Jilin hub loop. The report's economic rate of return was 8.4 per cent at completion against 6.2 per cent at appraisal, counting only the time passengers save against road and existing rail. All the figures are the Bank's own. The Independent Evaluation Group, the Bank's internal evaluators, also cut the borrower's performance from the report's Highly Satisfactory to Satisfactory, and gave as its grounds the underestimation of passenger traffic flows on the corridor and the two unfinished stations. No independent check was found.

The outcome ratings are already on the card, so only the borrower performance rating is given here. No non-Bank account of what the line delivered was found.

karnataka-state-highways-ii-compensation.whole: The Bank's completion report says the project financed capital improvement and maintenance works on 831 km of Karnataka's core road network. Its results table records 503 km completed under item-rate contracts against a revised target of 534 km, and 300 km under design-build-finance-operate-maintain-transfer concessions against a revised target of 301 km; 19 km was still unfinished at closing, 13 km held up by land acquisition and utility shifting and 6 km by works in progress. A further 1,078 km of non-rural roads were built as planned. It reports travel time on the project roads down 30 to 40 per cent against a target of 25 per cent, vehicle operating costs down 19 per cent against 15 per cent, and the share of the state's classified roads in good or fair condition up from 50 to 70 per cent, against a target the report's narrative gives as 65 per cent and its results table as 50 per cent. On the 62 km road safety demonstration corridor the report records deaths down 41 per cent against a target of 30 per cent and 143 accident blackspots treated in 2018-19; it gives the fall in accidents as 60 per cent in one passage and 66 per cent in another. The state raised US$416.56 million from private lenders against a revised target of US$400 million and an original target of US$500 million. Of that, the state road development corporation mobilised about US$97 million, which the report puts at about 60 per cent of the construction cost of the concession roads; the remaining 40 per cent was paid up front, in equal parts from the Bank loan and from a commercial bank. The project generated about 0.83 million days of unskilled work, 69 per cent of it going to local workers and 17 per cent to women. All these figures are the Bank's own. The report's economic rate of return was 32 per cent at completion against 30 per cent at appraisal, covering 97 per cent of project cost and built from vehicle operating cost savings, travel time savings and lower maintenance costs, and the Independent Evaluation Group, the Bank's internal evaluators, gave the same outcome, Bank performance and monitoring ratings as the report. No independent check was found.
karnataka-state-highways-ii-compensation.searched: World Bank completion report of 23 October 2019 for P107649 and the Independent Evaluation Group's ICR Review of 30 December 2019, both read from the PDFs. The land acquisition shortfalls are already on the card and are not repeated here. No non-Bank account of what the roads delivered was found.

liaoning-medium-cities-resettlement.whole: Across the six municipalities the Bank's completion report counts 107 km of road and six bridges built or rebuilt, less than planned because the local governments completed some sections with their own funds. It also counts about 4,478,000 square metres of road surface and footway repaired, traffic lights along 156 km, drainage along 107 km, 824 traffic monitoring and control installations, 141 sets of maintenance equipment, and for public transport 20 bus priority lines, 11 depots, 196 stops and shelters and 112 buses bought in Panjin. It reports travel times on monitored routes down by between 13 and 68 per cent, the share of city roads in good condition up from a range of 41 to 60 per cent before the project to 70 to 89 per cent after, and bus passenger numbers up by between 21 per cent in Fushun and 281 per cent in Panjin. Traffic deaths per 10,000 vehicles fell by 15 per cent in Liaoyang, from 3.3 to 2.8, and by 70 per cent in Jinzhou, from 4.3 to 1.3. One part of the project largely did not happen: only Jinzhou put road maintenance out to competitive tender, the other cities used limited bidding with municipally owned construction companies, and the Independent Evaluation Group, the Bank's internal evaluators, rated that objective Modest, finding the project made few improvements to road maintenance. Spending came to US$397.4 million against US$525.4 million estimated at appraisal. The report's economic rate of return was 22.7 per cent at completion against 15.2 per cent at appraisal, but the completion figure was calculated over roads accounting for 41 per cent of project cost against 70 per cent for the appraisal estimate, so the two are not measured over the same thing. All the figures are the Bank's own. No independent check was found.

liuzhan-railway-resettlement.whole: The project double-tracked and upgraded the existing single-track electrified railway between Liupanshui and Zhanyi, across three mountains over 6,000 feet high. The Bank's completion report counts 97 km of track laid in Guizhou, including 62.3 km of tunnel and 15.7 km of bridge and viaduct, with two new and seven rebuilt stations, and 99.7 km in Yunnan, including 10.7 km of tunnel and 9.2 km of bridge. It reports freight train speeds up from 23 to 70 km/h against a target of 41, express passenger speeds up from 55 to 100 km/h against a target of 90, and trains up from 31 to 45 pairs a day by October 2014, four months after the loan closed, against a target of 50 pairs after the first full year. Spending came to US$1,541.6 million against US$1,120.2 million estimated at appraisal, 40 per cent more, which the report attributes to higher construction costs, change orders and the renovation of 14 existing stations that had not been costed. Its economic rate of return was 13 per cent at completion against 17 per cent at appraisal, each covering the whole project. All these figures are the Bank's own. No independent check was found.

lucknow-muzaffarpur-highway-land.whole: By the World Bank's own count, 328 km of NH-28 were upgraded to a four-lane divided road, after the length was cut from the 483 km planned at approval. Travel time fell 23 per cent for cars and 25 per cent for trucks against a 20 per cent target, and fatal accidents across the corridor fell 36 per cent against a 10 per cent target; the 10 per cent cut targeted in truck operating costs was reached in none of the three sections, and on the Ayodhya-Gorakhpur section fatal accidents rose from 22 in the 2002 baseline year to 43. The completion report put the economic rate of return at 26.2 per cent for the 327 km finally built, against 26 per cent estimated at appraisal for the full 483 km; it counts savings in vehicle operating costs and in travel time for passengers and goods, and leaves accident savings out. The Bank's Independent Evaluation Group rated the outcome Unsatisfactory and Bank performance Unsatisfactory, each a step below the completion report's rating, and rated the quality of the project's monitoring Negligible. All of these figures come from the World Bank's own documents; no independent check of them was found.
lucknow-muzaffarpur-highway-land.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR2475 (13 December 2012), results table, paras 49-63 and Annex 3; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR14100 (posted 5 February 2014), ratings table. Both read from the document text on disk. No non-Bank source with output figures was found.

mekenajo-dembidolo-road-coffee.whole: By the World Bank's own count, the programme upgraded 302 km of narrow gravel road to asphalt, against the 391 km targeted, after the 89 km Ankober-Dulecha-Awash Arba road was dropped in 2015 over procurement and construction delays. On the Mekenajo-Dembidolo road, recorded at 181 km, traffic rose 330 per cent after the upgrade, average travel time fell from 2.5 minutes a kilometre in 2009 to 1 minute in 2017, and waiting time for minibuses fell from 112.6 minutes in 2012 to 23.5 minutes in 2016. The completion report put that road's economic rate of return at 21.5 per cent after the event against 14.8 per cent estimated for it at appraisal, counting savings in vehicle operating costs and travel time; the road contracts were finished before closing but overran their budgets by about 30 per cent and their time by about 140 per cent on average. The completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group both rated the outcome Moderately Satisfactory; the Group rated the quality of monitoring Modest against the report's Substantial, and rated efficiency Modest against the report's Substantial, citing the dropped road and the cost overruns. All of these figures come from the World Bank's own documents; no independent check of them was found.
mekenajo-dembidolo-road-coffee.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00004205 (1 June 2018), paras 16, 22-23, results framework and Annex 4; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR0021231, efficacy, efficiency and ratings sections. Both read from the document text on disk. The Group's efficacy section gives the Mekenajo-Dembidolo baseline travel time as 3 minutes a kilometre and the Welkite-Hosaina baseline as 2.5; the completion report and its results framework give the reverse, and the report's figures are used here. No non-Bank source with output figures was found.

naji-youjiang-waterways-resettlement.whole: By the World Bank's own count, the Naji complex delivered a shiplock and a hydropower station whose capacity was raised in design from the 57 megawatts set at appraisal to 66 megawatts, with three turbines completed on schedule in 2008. The plant generated 227 GWh in 2009, 10.2 per cent below that year's 253 GWh target, which the completion report attributes to a drought and to a delay in filling the reservoir caused partly by resettlement work; it expected an annual average of 273 GWh or more afterwards. Waterway freight between Baise and Nanning reached 2.396 million tonnes in 2009, against 0.814 million tonnes in 2003 and a 2009 target of 2.180 million tonnes, and average vessel size rose from 97 to 144.7 deadweight tonnes against a target of 152. The report put the Guangxi component's economic rate of return at 15.8 per cent at completion against 18 per cent at appraisal, counting savings in transport cost per tonne and the value of the electricity generated, and noted that no document trail survived for checking the detailed appraisal assumptions; the financial rate of return fell from the 3.4 per cent estimated at appraisal to 0.74 per cent after the provincial government decided to charge no shiplock fee along the Xijiang in Guangxi and the sale price of power to the grid was fixed at RMB 0.29 per kWh against the RMB 0.35 assumed. The report records income per head of farmers in Tianyang County rising from RMB 1,923 in 2004 to RMB 3,579 in 2009; the Independent Evaluation Group says it is not clear how much of that can be attributed to the project. All of these figures come from the World Bank's own documents; no independent check of them was found.
naji-youjiang-waterways-resettlement.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR1376 for P077137 (28 December 2011), paras on Guangxi outputs, economic and financial analysis and poverty impact; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR13857 (posted 14 January 2013), efficacy and efficiency sections. Both read from the document text on disk. No non-Bank source with output figures was found.

nanguang-railway-resettlement.whole: By the World Bank's own count, the project built about 400 km of new double-track electrified railway between Litang West and New Zhaoqing, plus two tracks of a 62 km four-track line on to Sanyanqiao, with about 94 million man-days of construction work; about 15 per cent of those man-days went to local labour, most of it hired in Guangxi rather than in the richer Guangdong. Passenger train pairs between Sanyanqiao and Litang West rose from seven in 2008 to 31 at closing in 2015 against a target of 20, and average travel time fell from 620 minutes to 156 minutes against a target of 170; the eight pairs of freight trains targeted never ran, because China Railway decided to use the line for passengers as part of a network-wide strategy. The completion report put the economic rate of return at 16 per cent after the event against 13 per cent at appraisal, counting passenger and freight travel-time savings, shorter distances and modelled 'agglomeration' effects worked out with an approach developed by the United Kingdom's Department for Transport; about half the counted benefit came from those agglomeration effects, and the report's own figures without them are 11 per cent after the event against 9 per cent at appraisal. The Independent Evaluation Group, which travelled the line in March 2018, recalculated the return with the agglomeration effects cut by 30 per cent and got 14.1 per cent, and wrote that the project's own benefits cannot be disentangled from those of the wider rail network it was joined to. All of these figures come from the World Bank's own documents; no independent check of them was found.
nanguang-railway-resettlement.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00003432 for P112359 (3 December 2015), paras 40-49, Annex 1 and Annex 3; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR0020097; Group Project Performance Assessment Report No. 127580 (2018), chapters 4 and 5. All read from the document text on disk. No non-Bank source with output figures was found.

nhiip-india-corridor-land-acquisition.whole: By the World Bank's own count, average travel time on the project roads fell from 2 minutes a kilometre to 1.17 for cars and from 3 minutes to 1.7 for trucks, both better than target, and recorded road deaths fell 45 per cent from a baseline of 163 in 2009. Vehicle operating costs fell from Rs 8 to Rs 7.2 a kilometre for cars and from Rs 14 to Rs 12.6 for trucks, exactly the target figures; the Bank's Independent Evaluation Group says there is not enough evidence that those figures were cross-checked against other data. The completion report put the economic rate of return at 20.3 per cent for the eight road sections built, totalling 617.3 km, against 25.74 per cent estimated at appraisal for 1,200 km of road in eleven sections; it counts savings in vehicle operating costs, maintenance costs and travel time, and gives contract award and implementation delays, lower traffic and higher contract costs as the reasons for the drop. A road safety enforcement pilot whose budget was raised at restructuring from US$17.5 million to US$72.5 million spent US$3.2 million, and the Group concludes the pilot was not carried out; the Group also says the reported rise in the share of state roads in good and fair condition cannot be fully attributed to the project, because the classified network itself grew from 37,501 km to 87,995 km. All of these figures come from the World Bank's own documents; no independent check of them was found.
nhiip-india-corridor-land-acquisition.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00005937 for P121185 (29 June 2022); Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR0023078 (21 February 2023), efficacy, efficiency and ICR quality sections. Both read from the document text on disk. The Group's ICR quality section puts the road safety allocation at US$55 million while its efficacy section gives the revised component cost as US$72.50 million; the component figure is used here. No non-Bank source with output figures was found.

orissa-state-roads-compensation.whole: Two of the project's six roads were finished. On those two the Bank's own measurement shows vehicle speeds up 32.5 per cent against a 36 per cent target, and no data at all were collected on vehicle operating cost savings; the project delivered a road asset management system the state was using at closing to plan road maintenance budgets, a road network master plan, a road safety policy and action plan, and a completed study on creating a road fund, while the road sector policy was written but not adopted and no road fund was set up. The economic rate of return for the two completed roads was 19.4 per cent for Khariar-Bhawanipatna and 18.6 per cent for the Berhampur-Taptapani section, against 22.3 and 15.4 per cent estimated at appraisal for the corridors they belonged to; it counts savings in vehicle operating costs, travel time, distance on bypasses and maintenance, and construction unit costs came out 1.60 and 1.81 times the appraisal estimate while annual traffic growth came out 1.73 and 2.93 times it. The Bank's Independent Evaluation Group rated the project's achievement of its objective Negligible and the outcome Unsatisfactory, against the completion report's Moderately Unsatisfactory, and rated the risk to the result Substantial against the report's Modest, writing that the project did not remove transport bottlenecks in the targeted corridor, that there is no evidence congestion was reduced, and that the effect on investment and on economic and social development was never measured. All of these figures come from the World Bank's own documents; no independent check of them was found.
orissa-state-roads-compensation.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00003903 for P096023 (February 2017), ratings sheet, paras 53-63 and Annex 3; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR0020654 (21 June 2017), efficacy, efficiency, outcome and ratings sections. Both read from the document text on disk. Two defects in the Group's review are not used here: its ratings table prints the completion report's outcome rating as Unsatisfactory where the report itself gives Moderately Unsatisfactory, and its efficiency text states 'The overall ex-post ERR was 25.1 percent compared to the ex-ante ERR of 18.6 percent', the reverse of its own table (appraisal 25.10, completion 18.60) and of the report, so only the per-road figures both documents agree on are given. No non-Bank source with output figures was found.

shaanxi-ankang-road-resettlement.whole: By the World Bank's own count, the project built an 87 km expressway from Ankang to Maoba and rehabilitated 106 local roads totalling 1,391.57 km, against 108 roads and 1,480 km expected at appraisal. Travel time from Ankang to Maoba fell from 3.8 hours on the parallel existing highways to 1 hour, and daily traffic on the sample county and township roads rose from 243 vehicles in 2009 to 508 in 2012. Annual average daily traffic on the new expressway was 3,049 vehicles in 2012 against a target of 5,870 to 6,360, after toll stations on the parallel S310 and G210 were removed in 2011; the expressway recorded 126 accidents in 2012 against a target of 35, and 2 fatal accidents against a target of 13. The completion report put the economic rate of return at 15.3 per cent for the whole project at completion, 15.0 per cent for the expressway and 18.5 per cent for the local roads; the Independent Evaluation Group gives the appraisal estimate as 17.9 per cent, says the return counts savings in vehicle operating cost and in passenger travel time, and records the expressway's actual cost at US$1,096 million, 95 per cent above the US$561 million base cost estimated for it at appraisal. All of these figures come from the World Bank's own documents; no independent check of them was found.
shaanxi-ankang-road-resettlement.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR2142 for P075613 (13 June 2013), results sheet, paras on outputs, traffic, accidents and efficiency, and Annex 6; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR14449 (22 September 2014), outputs, efficiency and ratings sections. Both read from the document text on disk. The expressway length is the completion report's 87 km, which the Group's own component description also gives as 'about 87km'; one output bullet in the Group's review prints 78 km. The completion report also notes a forecast that the expressway would reach its target volume of about 6,585 vehicles a day in 2018. No non-Bank source with output figures was found.

shiyan-connecting-road-safeguards.whole: By the World Bank's own count, the project built the 106.4 km four-lane Shiyan-Manchuanguan Expressway, opened to traffic in December 2007 with the tunnel at the Shaanxi border opening in October 2009, together with three local roads totalling 262 km and the 355 metre Jiangjunhe bridge, which replaced an old bridge usable only by single trucks and cars. All three local roads had been earth roads of the lowest class; the two monitored for the project had been closed 45 and 90 days a year at the start, and bus service frequency on the local roads rose four to five times. Traffic on the expressway reached 6,600 to 8,700 vehicles a day in early 2010, four to ten times the level at the end of 2008, and every expressway counting section met its traffic target; the fatal accident rate on NH316 and the expressway fell from 3.4 per 100,000 vehicle-km in 2004 to 2.1 by the end of 2009, against a target of 2.9. The completion report put the economic rate of return at 19 per cent for the whole project against 17 per cent at appraisal, with 34 per cent against 24 per cent for the local roads programme, counting reductions in vehicle operating costs, travel time costs and maintenance costs over 24 years. The report records an 80 per cent rise in the counties' GDP alongside the local roads, and the Bank's Independent Evaluation Group repeats the figure and says the improvements were not wholly due to the road upgrading. All of these figures come from the World Bank's own documents; no independent check of them was found.
shiyan-connecting-road-safeguards.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00001409 for P081749, results sheet indicators 1-4, paras on local mobility, road safety and efficiency, and Annexes 2 and 3; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR13442, outcome and ratings sections. Both read from the document text on disk. The report's narrative gives an interim accident rate of 3.1 for 2008 'per million veh-km'; the results sheet gives the unit as per 100,000 vehicle-km and the completion value as 2.1, which is used here. No non-Bank source with output figures was found.

shizheng-railway-resettlement.whole: By the World Bank's own count, the project built 355 km of new double-track high-speed passenger railway between Shijiazhuang and Zhengzhou, six new stations at Gaoyi, Xingtai, Handan, Anyang, Hebi and Xinxiang, and bought 28 catenary maintenance vehicles; the Independent Evaluation Group counts eight stations along the line, including Shijiazhuang and Zhengzhou, which the completion report says were not part of the project. Travel time for non-stop high-speed trains fell from 198 minutes before the project to 81 minutes, better than the 85-minute target, and passenger density on the corridor rose from 61 million passenger-km per route-km in 2012 to 75 million in 2014, of which the new line carried 23 million. The corridor carried 180 train pairs a day in 2015 against 181 forecast at appraisal, but with 60 high-speed pairs rather than the 100 assumed, because China Railway kept about 65 conventional trains running in response to public feedback on fares and on access to intermediate stations; trains ran at 310 km/h rather than the 350 km/h first operated, mainly to cut energy use. The completion report put the economic rate of return at 15 per cent against 20 per cent at appraisal, counting passenger and freight travel-time savings and externalities in carbon emissions and reduced accidents, with agglomeration benefits left out to match the appraisal method. The Evaluation Group rated the risk to the result Modest against the report's Negligible, judging the social risk modest because passenger attitude surveys may not have captured what people will actually pay. All of these figures come from the World Bank's own documents; no independent check of them was found.
shizheng-railway-resettlement.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00003435 for P099062 (18 October 2016), results sheet, paras 40-48, Annexes 2 and 3; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR0020495 (8 March 2017), outputs, risk and ratings sections. Both read from the document text on disk. No non-Bank source with output figures was found.

vietnam-distribution-efficiency-five-hou.whole: By the World Bank's own count, the project built 4,001 km of new low-voltage line against 2,446 km planned and 1,146.75 km of new 110 kV line against 924.5 km planned, rebuilt 3,429 km of old low-voltage line against 4,062 km planned, and added 3,135 MVA of new 110 kV substation capacity against 2,351 MVA planned; it carried out 177 subprojects against the 99 planned at appraisal, with savings from competitive bidding put back into more work. The Independent Evaluation Group records distribution losses falling by between 1.6 and 7.5 percentage points more than targeted across the five power corporations, and avoided emissions of 365,707 tonnes of CO2 a year against a 269,148 tonne target; metered customers cut consumption past target in each corporation, by 448.5 GWh a year against a 414.5 GWh target in the Northern Power Corporation. The completion report put the economic rate of return at 38.3 per cent for the whole project at completion against 29.2 per cent calculated at appraisal for the first-phase subprojects only, and the financial return to the power companies at 19.7 per cent against 16.7 per cent, crediting lower investment costs, better system efficiency and a slightly wider margin between the bulk supply tariff and the average retail tariff. The Group notes that the report does not discuss what the rises in retail electricity tariffs meant for households, and quotes a Bank study finding that nominal average tariffs rose 53 per cent between January 2015 and January 2019 while cumulative inflation over the same period was about 56 per cent. All of these figures come from the World Bank's own documents; no independent check of them was found.
vietnam-distribution-efficiency-five-hou.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00004664 for P125996 (14 June 2019), results tables, key outputs by component and Annex 4; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR0021771 (21 January 2020), efficacy, efficiency and ratings sections. Both read from the document text on disk. The quoted tariff sentence, from a forthcoming Bank study by Lee and Gerner, prints its two dates in reverse order ('from January 2019 to January 2015'). No non-Bank source with output figures was found.

vietnam-rural-energy-2-land-loss.whole: By the World Bank's own count, the project installed 27,700 circuit km of low-voltage line against a revised 32,000 km target, 5,300 circuit km of medium-voltage line against 4,300 targeted, 700 MVA of transformer capacity against 1,100 targeted, and 1,915,000 household meters against 2,700,000 targeted. Household access to electricity in the project provinces rose from 60 to 98 per cent against a revised 90 per cent target, with 325,000 households in remote rural areas connected across 25 provinces; average distribution losses in the rural low-voltage system fell from 30 to 10 per cent, and recorded carbon savings were 365,000 tonnes against a revised 310,000 tonne target. The economic rate of return was 17.5 per cent at closure against 18.2 per cent at appraisal, both worked out for the same first-phase investments in 355 communes in six provinces, counting lower losses, less spent by customers on equipment to cope with poor supply, the gain from switching to cheaper grid power and extra sales; the investment cost per household rose from US$578 in 2005 to US$1,062 in 2009. The project's stated objective was to improve access to good quality, affordable electricity for rural communities in support of Vietnam's socio-economic development, and the Bank's Independent Evaluation Group records that no study was carried out at closure to assess the project's effect on the socio-economic development of rural communities in the selected provinces, the completion report citing instead a 2011 study of rural electrification in Vietnam as a whole. All of these figures come from the World Bank's own documents; no independent check of them was found.
vietnam-rural-energy-2-land-loss.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00003194 for P074688; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR14722 (posted 12 May 2015), objective, outputs, outcomes, efficiency and ratings sections. Both read from the document text on disk. No non-Bank source with output figures was found.

vietnam-water-resources-assistance-reset.whole: By the World Bank's own count, the project rehabilitated and modernised six irrigation schemes, about 5 per cent of the command area of Vietnam's 75 irrigation schemes, under 295 construction contracts; the average share of a scheme's command area actually irrigated rose from 50 to 81 per cent against a 75 per cent target, and annual crop production rose 31 per cent for paddy, 41 per cent for maize, 52 per cent for soybean and 94 per cent for vegetables. It also set up a dam safety unit covering all dams under the agriculture ministry, which oversees about 95 per cent of Vietnam's dams, carried out remedial safety works on four dams, piloted dam safety instrumentation on one dam and issued a national dam safety regulation. The completion report put the economic rate of return at 15.3 per cent counting agricultural benefits from the irrigation component, 88 per cent of project costs, and at 27.7 per cent when municipal and industrial water use was added for all the schemes, against 14.7 per cent at appraisal; income on a typical 0.25 hectare fully gravity-irrigated farm rose from about D0.96 million (US$46) a year to D2.15 million (US$103). The Bank's Independent Evaluation Group wrote that much of the production increase came from the larger irrigated area rather than from the modernisation the project was built around, several modernisation measures being finished only in the project's last year; its 2019 field assessment records a one-third reduction in the infrastructure improvements actually completed against what was planned, and says the productivity gains relied partly on the government's own agricultural extension programme. All of these figures come from the World Bank's own documents; no independent check of them was found.
vietnam-water-resources-assistance-reset.searched: Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR14273 for P065898 (posted 9 December 2013), efficacy, efficiency and ratings sections; Group Project Performance Assessment Report No. 138389 (2019), chapters 4 and 5 and the three-column ratings table. Both read from the document text on disk; the project's own completion report (ICR00002604) is not among the case's sources and its ratings are taken from the assessment's table. No non-Bank source with output figures was found.
